name: basement-membrane-v1
title: Basement membrane v1 — collagen IV network modulus & remodelling for the AICS vertex model
description:
This investigation is the clean-room Vivarium build of the AICS-Lumenoids
"Basement membrane — v1 model specification" (Roam graph, exported 2026-09-29;
the source spec and diagram are in `workspace/references/`). We do not have the
authors' LAMMPS/Smoldyn decks, so every model parameter is transcribed from the
spec's parameter sheet and clearly labelled as such.

**Engines.** The workspace imports two already-wrapped simulators —
`viva-lammps` (the `LAMMPSProcess` bridge) and `viva-smoldyn` — and builds the
collagen IV network on top of the real LAMMPS engine. LAMMPS runs stages 1–2
(rigid rods, junction flexibility); Smoldyn is held for stage 3 (flexible
fibers + surface binders) per spec decision #2.

**Staged build (spec "v1 build").**
  - Stage 1 — reproduce the paper; separate elastic from viscous. Stretch,
    hold, then switch the crosslink chemistry on. Reports an elastic modulus
    and a stress-relaxation time.  ← this investigation's first study.
  - Stage 2 — growing substrate (flat): impose equibiaxial strain rate ε̇,
    read off σ(ε̇); an effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ and the rate at which the
    response turns elastic.
  - Stage 3 — add the cell–BM linker (surface-attached springs, constant
    off-rate). Smoldyn's surface binders land here.
  - Stage 4 — curvature (only if stages 2–3 depend on R beyond ε̇ = Ṙ/R).

**Coupling route (spec decision).** Offline first: tabulate the BM's modulus
and remodelling time against growth rate and hand them to the vertex model.
Then direct: vertex-mesh surface velocities drive the BM substrate, BM stress
feeds back, exchanged every N vertex steps.

at_a_glance.role: Stage 1. Assemble → equilibrate → stretch → hold(elastic) → hold(breakage- only, viscous). Elastic modulus is consistent with zero (z < 4, floppy); the remodelling mechanism is correct but τ is below detection at v1 scale.
Stage 2. Sweep the equibiaxial strain rate ε̇ on the growing substrate and read σ(ε̇) → the effective viscosity η and the viscous→elastic crossover.

Follow-up. Rigidity-percolation sweep: raising crosslink connectivity (z up to 3.7) never reaches z = 4 and never rigidifies — proving stiffness needs junction bending / bundling, not more crosslinks.

Follow-up (FP1). Implements junction bending (fix restrain, as-formed angles) + an athermal modulus. Bending dominates the mechanics (floppy → large |E|), confirming it governs stiffness — but a reproducible modulus needs a larger, pre-stress-free network (v2).

Geometric readouts (spec "has: geometrical structure"). Reads porosity + bundling off the real network against measured BM. Pore diameter reaches the corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at realistic density; the NC1/7S-only topology under-bundles (mean ~1 protomer/strand, below the measured 5–7), because the released model has no lateral-association bond. Carries the evidence map.

glossary.definition: One collagen IV triple-helical molecule (~376 nm end-to-end); modelled as one two-bead rod.
The two crosslinking ends of a protomer. NC1 binds 1 partner (hexamer), 7S binds 3 (tetramer/spider).
The viscous stress-relaxation time set by crosslink make/break kinetics; calibrated to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime.
Equibiaxial in-plane strain rate. A sphere of radius R growing at Ṙ stretches its shell at ε̇ = Ṙ/R.

question: What effective elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time does a coarse-grained collagen IV basement-membrane network produce on a growing (biaxially stretching) boundary — the two numbers the AICS 3D vertex model needs to couple to a basement membrane?
hypothesis: A standalone collagen IV network, coarse-grained at the fiber scale (one protomer = one two-bead rod, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume), reproduces the Meadowcroft/Barrientos regime: a very soft elastic modulus (the published network's own linear modulus is ≈0.03 Pa) and a crosslink- turnover-limited stress-relaxation time that can be calibrated to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime. Its effective modulus and remodelling time, tabulated against growth rate ε̇, become inputs to the vertex model (offline coupling first).

acceptance_criteria.behavior: The staged protocol runs end-to-end on real LAMMPS, a crosslinked network assembles from two-bead rods, the stress-strain ramp yields a finite (very soft) elastic modulus, and the chemistry-on hold shows a measurable stress relaxation, or a noise-limited null at v1 network size.
The ε̇ sweep runs and returns σ(ε̇) and an effective viscosity η per rate, with the viscous and elastic regimes identified at v1 parameters.
The connectivity sweep shows z stays below 4 and the modulus stays consistent with zero, establishing that rigidity requires junction bending / bundling.
Junction bending is implemented and dominates the mechanics (floppy baseline ~0 → large |E|); a reproducible modulus is blocked on network size and a pre-stress-free measurement.

executive.what_is_this: The first Vivarium build of the AICS lumenoid basement membrane: a coarse- grained collagen IV network on a moving boundary, run until it reports an elastic modulus and a remodelling time for the vertex model.
executive.verdict: Infrastructure stood up and stages 1–2 run on real LAMMPS. Hardening produced a mechanistic result: the network's elastic modulus is consistent with zero (−0.03 ± 0.06 over a seed ensemble) because its mean coordination z ≤ 3 is below the 2D rigidity threshold z = 4 — it is floppy by the spec's connectivity, matching the published ≈0.03 Pa. The rigidity sweep (bm-v3) confirms more crosslinks cannot fix this (z tops out at 3.7): stiffness requires junction bending / bundling. FP1 (bm-v4) then implemented junction bending and confirmed it — bending dominates the mechanics (floppy E≈0 → |E| tens–hundreds) — but the modulus is ill-conditioned at v1 network size, so it is not yet calibratable; a reproducible value needs a larger, pre-stress-free network (fp3). The remodelling mechanism was corrected (a fix-bond/break densification artifact → a force- independent off-rate), so stress now relaxes correctly, but τ is below detection while the network is floppy. Absolute pascals and a calibrated τ await the reproducible bending modulus + the energy-scale decision.
decisions_needed: Engine for stages 1–2: LAMMPS now; revisit Smoldyn at stage 3 (spec #2).
Secretion: fixed concentration vs fixed flux (spec #3).
Energy scale: report modulus in Pa (fit to a measured modulus) or keep kT and report a ratio (spec #4).
Coupling contract: which vertex-model term receives the BM — basal tension, mobility, or elastic spring (spec #5).
Linker values: density, spring constant, off-rate; sweep off-rate as a multiple of the crosslink break rate (spec #6).
Growth rate ε̇ from the lumenoid radius time course — still requested (spec #7).
Slab thickness / layer count — one z-stack away (spec #9).
Which readout calibrates vs validates — remodelling time calibrates MP and the time unit, so it cannot also validate (spec #10).

studies.name: bm-v1-stage1-modulus-remodelling
studies.question: Can the clean-room collagen IV network separate an elastic modulus from a viscous remodelling time, as the paper's staged protocol does?

resolved_uncertainties: The viscous 'relaxation' densification was a fix-bond/break artifact — root-caused and fixed.
The ~0 modulus is rigidity-percolation physics (z < 4), not a measurement failure.
remaining_uncertainties: τ (remodelling time) — below detection until the network is rigid.
Absolute modulus in pascals — energy scale still open (spec #4).

followup_study_proposals.title: Off-rate → τ calibration to the ≈20 h lifetime

findings.statement: LAMMPS `fix bond/break` models only OVER-STRETCH breaking, not a force- independent off-rate — small Rmax dissolves the network, large Rmax saturates it. Replacing it with a controlled random-deletion off-rate gives a make/break steady state and crosslink turnover.

evidence.observed: crosslinks 45→401 (old, densifies) vs steady ~54 then decay 46→3 (off-rate)

findings.explanation: Breaking must be length-independent to be a controllable rate (spec: force-independent in v1).
findings.next_action: adopted in viva_lumenoid/collagen.py; guarded by a regression test

findings.statement: The v1 central-force network is below the 2D rigidity threshold (mean z ≤ 3 < 4), so its elastic modulus is statistically consistent with zero — matching the published ≈0.03 Pa.

evidence.observed: modulus −0.03 ± 0.06 LJ (95% CI, 6 seeds); mean z ≈ 1.2; z_max = 3

findings.explanation: Maxwell counting: NC1 beads reach z = 2, 7S beads z = 4, mean ≤ 3 < 4 → floppy regardless of crosslink density. Rigidity must come from bending / bundling.

findings.statement: The remodelling mechanism is now correct (stress decays as crosslinks break), but the relaxable stress is small in a floppy network, so τ is below detection at v1 scale.

evidence.observed: ensemble viscous decay ~0.29→0.25; s0 < 2·noise → τ unresolved

findings.next_action: resolve on a rigid (bending) network or a much larger ensemble

studies.claim: A coarse-grained collagen IV network (two-bead rods, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume) run through the spec's stage-1 protocol — stretch, hold, then switch the chemistry on — yields a separable elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time on real LAMMPS.

biological_validation.basis: Consistent with the published ≈0.03 Pa (near-floppy) modulus; the floppiness is mechanistically explained by connectivity (z < 4).

regression_compatibility.basis: No upstream regression baseline for this clean-room build.

explanatory_gain.basis: Identifies WHY the BM network is soft — connectivity below rigidity percolation — telling the vertex model that BM stiffness comes from bending/bundling, not crosslink count.

derived.insight: LAMMPS `fix bond/break` models only OVER-STRETCH breaking, not a force- independent off-rate — small Rmax dissolves the network, large Rmax saturates it. Replacing it with a controlled random-deletion off-rate gives a make/break steady state and crosslink turnover.

studies.name: bm-v2-stress-vs-strainrate
studies.question: What is σ(ε̇), and where does the network cross from viscous to elastic?
studies.claim: Imposing an equibiaxial in-plane strain rate ε̇ on the growing collagen IV network and reading the steady-state stress σ(ε̇) gives the effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ (viscous at slow rates) and the rate at which the response turns elastic — the σ(ε̇) relation the vertex model needs.

studies.name: bm-v3-junction-bending-rigidity
studies.question: Can more crosslink connectivity rigidify the v1 network, or is bending required?

findings.statement: Raising NC1/7S crosslinks lifts z to only ~3.7 (never 4), and the modulus stays consistent with zero throughout — central-force connectivity cannot rigidify the v1 sheet.

expected.range: rigid only for z ≥ 4 (2D central-force isostatic point)

findings.explanation: NC1×1 + 7S×3 caps z at 3; bundling raises it but the geometry saturates below 4.
findings.next_action: implement junction bending (fix bond/create atype + angle_style) — the load-bearing v2 fix

studies.claim: The v1 collagen IV network's ~zero elastic modulus is a rigidity-percolation effect: with NC1×1 + 7S×3 connectivity the mean coordination z ≤ 3 stays below the 2D central-force isostatic point z = 4, so raising crosslink connectivity alone cannot rigidify it — a measurable modulus needs junction bending (or true bundling bonds).

derived.insight: Raising NC1/7S crosslinks lifts z to only ~3.7 (never 4), and the modulus stays consistent with zero throughout — central-force connectivity cannot rigidify the v1 sheet.

studies.name: bm-v4-junction-bending
studies.question: Does junction bending yield the measurable modulus the vertex model needs?

resolved_uncertainties: Bending, not crosslink connectivity, governs this network's stiffness (confirmed qualitatively).
The athermal minimisation measures the floppy modulus deterministically (removes the dynamic-measurement noise).
remaining_uncertainties: A reproducible, calibratable bending modulus — blocked on network size + pre-stress-free measurement.

findings.statement: Junction bending is implemented as `fix restrain` pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (per-junction rest angle avoids the single-rest-angle frustration), with an auto-reduced timestep and an athermal energy-minimised modulus readout.

evidence.observed: floppy modulus measured as E ≈ 0 (deterministic) via minimisation

findings.statement: Bending dominates the mechanics (|E| jumps to tens–hundreds, network no longer floppy) but the modulus is ill-conditioned at v1 size — it scatters and sign-flips across seeds (pathological near-degenerate minima), so it is not yet a calibratable value.
findings.explanation: The stiff, pre-stressed, disordered small network has many near-degenerate energy minima; the equibiaxial-stress modulus is dominated by pre-stress and finite-size buckling rather than the intrinsic shear modulus.
findings.next_action: seed v2: larger network (self-averaging) + pre-stress-free reference

studies.claim: Junction bending (harmonic angle restraints pinned to each crosslink's as-formed geometry) is the constraint that governs the network's stiffness; bm-v3 showed crosslink connectivity alone cannot (z < 4). Adding bending dominates the mechanics, but a reproducible elastic modulus is not obtainable at v1 network size.

derived.insight: Junction bending is implemented as `fix restrain` pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (per-junction rest angle avoids the single-rest-angle frustration), with an auto-reduced timestep and an athermal energy-minimised modulus readout.

studies.name: bm-v5-porosity-bundling
studies.question: Does the v1 network reproduce the measured pore-size and bundling of a real BM?

findings.statement: Pore size scales with network density and reaches the corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at the densest sampled network (median 76 nm) — the mesh is realistic and pore size is a tunable density readout, not a free universal.

evidence.observed: median pore 130 → 108 → 120 → 76 nm as rods rise 150 → 500

expected.range: 72 ± 40 nm (corneal BM EM); 20–60 nm hydrated Matrigel

findings.explanation: Porosity is emergent from areal coverage; the comparator fixes a density.

findings.statement: The NC1/7S-only topology does not bundle: mean strand size stays near 1 (~82% singletons), below the 5–7 protomers per strand measured in the PFHR-9 scaffold. The model has no lateral-association bond.

evidence.observed: mean strand 1.03 → 1.17, max 5–7 occasionally, <5% of rods in 5–7 strands

findings.explanation: The released model bundles only through 7S branching; the lateral- association bond that builds strands is absent (spec: a lateral term would itself under-bundle ~2× if calibrated in vitro).
findings.next_action: add an explicit lateral-association bond (v2) and re-measure bundling

studies.claim: Of the two geometric readouts the spec asks the network to reproduce, one is met and one is not: the simulated pore-size distribution reaches the measured corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at realistic density, while the protomers-per- strand distribution stays near 1, below the measured 5–7. The released NC1/7S topology has no lateral-association bond, so it cannot form multi-protomer strands — a limitation the spec identifies in advance.

derived.insight: Pore size scales with network density and reaches the corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at the densest sampled network (median 76 nm) — the mesh is realistic and pore size is a tunable density readout, not a free universal.
